data.one_liner: Real native iOS UI elements driven by Flutter layout, with matching Flutter UI on Android.
data.what_it_does: Puts a native iOS overlay above the Flutter surface for navigation bars, tab bars, sheets, and glass effects while keeping them in sync with the Flutter layout every frame. On Android and older iOS, it renders matching Flutter replicas for cross-platform support.
use_when: You want native iOS UIKit bars, sheets, and Liquid Glass effects in a Flutter app
You need a single codebase to serve iOS and Android with platform-appropriate UI replicas
You want complex native messaging composers and search toolbars driven by Flutter widgets
avoid_when: You are building for Web or desktop (which are not supported)
You need a pure Material Design or Cupertino style without native iOS 26 overlays
strengths: Real native iOS 26 UIKit controls like UITabBarController and UINavigationBar
No platform views per widget, allowing glass widgets to merge and morph naturally
Consistent Flutter fallback replicas for Android and older iOS versions
weaknesses: Pre-release software (0.1 status) where APIs may change
Does not support Web or desktop platforms due to reliance on dart:ffi
data.setup_notes: Requires Flutter 3.47 or later (Dart 3.13) and iOS deployment target 15.0 or later. Voice recording requires an NSMicrophoneUsageDescription.
